terms.comment: Classically a fault or slip in writing (Cic. Verr. 2.2.104, Lewis & Short); applied here to a fault in a program. Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no word for a software bug: Traupman’s bug is the insect, cīmex (p. 284), and his mendum an error in writing (p. 310).

phrases.latin: Mendum est sīcut lapillus quī in calceō tuō latet: nōn bene ambulās, dōnec lapillum invēneris et ējēceris.
phrases.english: A bug is like a pebble hiding in your shoe: you can’t walk properly until you’ve found the pebble and thrown it out.
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

sources: Lewis & Short: mendum · Lewis & Short: menda
Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 284, 310.
